feasibility_reasoning: (1) React already yields. node_modules/@tanstack/react-start/dist/plugin/default-entry/client.tsx:5-12 wraps hydrateRoot in startTransition, so hydration is already time-sliced. That explains the ~169 vendor-react slices. tasks.py on lha1-mobile at ×4 shows only 6 slices over 12.5 ms obs (12.9–13.9 ms), adding about 20 ms of blocking. The TBT really comes from a handful of synchronous tasks: a 95.6 ms vendor-react commit with Layout (sim 191 ms, blocking 141), a 34.3 ms root pass, style recalcs of 40.5/40.4/32.4 ms, 35.5 ms 'other', a 37.3 ms React task containing ParseHTML, and a 23.5 ms timer. (2) React cannot time-slice a commit, and boundaries retried in the same lane can commit together. Splitting the commit therefore needs the hydration workstream's island gate (hydration.md §H7), and the cause of the forced Layout inside the commit is still unknown (hydration.md open question #1). (3) Deferral hazards. A Default/Sync update reaching a dehydrated island makes React client-render it: the SSR HTML is lost, the null public fallback shows (lazySuspense.tsx LazyFallback), and CLS follows. A transition (ThemeProvider.tsx:126, BuilderRenderer.tsx:255-258) waits until the island hydrates, with no upper bound if the trigger is interaction or visibility. Deferring mega menus contradicts lazyWidgets.tsx:35-36 ('navigation must hydrate first'). The device-switch <style> swaps come from the desktop-first parity design at BuilderRenderer.tsx:238-242. New Suspense boundaries around header or footer risk the streaming trap at lazyWidgets.tsx:50-58. The fixture cannot reveal refetch-driven updates because Supabase fails fast. (4) The gate is mis-specified. firstVisitMainThread.ts:28 observes only longtasks of 50 ms or more. Under CDP ×4 the durations are already scaled, so '4·dur−50' scales twice. Without throttling, the observer cannot see the 12.5–50 ms tasks. Real throttling also differs from Lantern because React yields on wall-clock time. No CPU throttling exists in e2e-performance today, and the first-visit.yml runner is shared and noisy. (5) The analyst's evidence overstates the mechanism. whatif.py:136-156 'cap' truncates tasks and deletes CPU, so the report's 'total CPU unchanged' is false. P_post50/P_cap12 also apply to every post-FCP task, not only the code LA-C1 touches. setTimeout(0) at router.tsx:210 is confirmed unchanged.
blocking_issues: The gate formula sum max(0,4·dur−50) over PerformanceObserver longtasks (firstVisitMainThread.ts:28) is wrong in both modes. Under CDP throttle ×4 it scales twice. Unthrottled, it cannot see tasks under 50 ms. Replace it with the Lantern formula over all top-level tasks of an unthrottled trace (×4, layout ×2, as tasks.py does), or with LHCI desktop cpuSlowdownMultiplier=4 plus mobile simulate in lighthouserc.json.

Hydration already runs in startTransition (default-entry/client.tsx:5-12). TBT is dominated by about 8 synchronous tasks: the 95.6 ms commit with forced Layout, the 34 ms root pass, style recalcs, the streamed-parse React task and a timer. 'Yield React work' targets slices that contribute about 20 ms. Before choosing a mechanism, find the cause of the forced Layout with a React profiling build.

A commit cannot be split without island gating. Any Default/Sync update reaching a suspended island makes React client-render it: SSR HTML is lost, the null fallback shows and CLS follows. Transitions wait without a bound while islands stay gated. A precondition test is required with a backend that returns data (the fixture fails fast and hides this).
Deferring mega-menu hydration contradicts the lazyWidgets.tsx:35-36 rule. The header must stay hydrated first, or that rule must be explicitly revised.
The fix for the device-switch <style> swaps must not add Vary on UA or client hints to the edge-cached document, because that would split the cache key and cost SI and TTFB.
The what-if evidence cap12 = 0 is truncation over all post-FCP tasks, not a model of yielding with CPU preserved. Re-baseline on several traces, since fixture TBT varies 558–991 ms between runs.
effect_reasoning: I re-ran Lantern on the analyst's lha1 trace with my own split.py (CPU-preserving split, unlike the analyst's truncating 'cap'), at h2 + 38 KB hero parity. Mobile ×4, base 356 ms: every post-FCP task ≤12 ms gives 0. React-only ≤12 plus removing style recalcs over 20 ms gives 22. React ≤16 plus style gives 93, React ≤20 plus style gives 187, and style alone gives 306. Desktop at ×4, base 444 ms: all ≤12 gives 44, React ≤12 plus style 150, ≤16 gives 290, ≤20 gives 332, style alone 434. Desktop at ×5, the analyst's own PSI-host estimate (base 765 ms): all ≤12 gives 129 and React ≤12 plus style gives 297, because a 12 ms piece becomes 60 ms simulated. The ≤110 desktop target is met only if non-React tasks are capped too. For PSI I used the analyst's split. Mobile 600 ms is hydration 55–65 %, gtag 20–30 % and consent about 10 %; gtag and consent are outside LA-C1. Removing 74–94 % of the hydration and style share leaves 240–360 ms, which score.py rates 60–64; with a ≤20 ms commit split it is about 430 ms and 57. Desktop 740 ms: the in-scope fixture part drops by 154–294 ms, and about 300 ms of production extras (gtag, consent, refetch, more DOM) remain, giving about 450–590 ms. The ×5 calibration gives about 300 ms plus gtag. So desktop lands at 300–590 ms, which score.py rates 73–84, not 95 (100 ms would give 95.3). The claim of 95 needs LA-2 as well. Moving hydration CPU out of the LH trace (islands deferred to interaction, consent shell) gives more than finer yield granularity.
corrected_estimate: Fixture: mobile ×4 TBT 356 → 22–93 ms (≤12–16 ms React cap plus style fix), or 187 at a ≤20 ms cap. Desktop at ×4: 444 → 150–290 ms (target ≤110 only if non-React tasks are capped too). PSI: mobile 600 → ~240–360 ms, score 60–64 (+7 to +11), and about 57 if the commit is split only to ~20 ms. Desktop 740 → ~300–590 ms, score 73–84 (+3 to +14), not 95. Desktop 95 needs LA-C1 plus LA-2 (gtag and consent) plus capping or deferring non-React work.
better_alternative: First profile and fix the forced Layout in the 95.6 ms hydration commit and the 34 ms root pass (worth ~228 ms of latent blocking at ×4), and the BuilderRenderer device-switch <style> swaps. Then defer below-fold islands, consent and overlays to interaction, which removes CPU from the LH trace. Do not build a general yielding framework first. As the gate, extend the existing lighthouserc.json/lighthouse.yml with a desktop collection at cpuSlowdownMultiplier=4 and a mobile simulate collection on the fixture, or compute Lantern blocking from an unthrottled CDP trace, instead of using longtask observers under CDP throttling.
